scope.population: 10454272 taker fills and 45849 wallets, restricted to wallets active in at least 2 windows; every cell repeated at each fill floor in [50, 100]

declared_not_confirmed.note: settings.py declares these; this run did not state what it used, so they are the declaration and not a property of this artifact

_meta.object: panel common-vs-idiosyncratic variance decomposition of per-counterparty 10s toxicity (trade-print mo10)
_meta.model: ybar_{i,t} = mu + c_t + a_i + u_{i,t}; common = Var(c_t), idiosyncratic = Var(a_i) after period demeaning, within = Var(u)
_meta.estimator: period FE for the common component; naive between-wallet variance of period-demeaned cell means (upward-biased) plus a split-half cross-wallet covariance bias correction Cov(aHat_A, aHat_B) (KSS-style, noise cancels) for the idiosyncratic component
_meta.seed_streams: split_seeds drive the covariance bias correction and come from master_seed; reliability_seeds drive the reliability diagnostic and come from reliability_seed_base; the permutation nulls draw their own seeds from master_seed
_meta.markout_sign: positive = taker profited = maker adversely selected (build convention)
_meta.interpretation_held: The markout reference is the TRADE-PRINT mo10, not a book mid, so the MAGNITUDE of the idiosyncratic wallet effect a_i mixes adverse selection with bid-ask bounce and the maker's earned spread (same caveat as i2_walletfe.py). This object decomposes the VARIANCE STRUCTURE into a market-wide-COMMON (period) component and a wallet-stable IDIOSYNCRATIC component; it does NOT claim the idiosyncratic magnitude is all adverse selection. The book-mid attribution of the magnitude is a documented follow-on. What the panel adds over i2 is the SEPARATION of the wallet-stable part from the market-wide-common part, impossible within a single window.
_meta.headline_note: HEADLINE = the PER-COIN split-half-corrected idiosyncratic share, and it is not one number: at the 50-fill floor 6.6% on BTC, 1.0% on ETH, 1.4% on SOL; at the 100-fill floor 29.8% on BTC, 1.4% on ETH, 2.0% on SOL. The POOLED cross-coin figure (1.3% at 50 fills, 1.6% at 100 fills) is a pooling / DENOMINATOR artifact and not the headline, though only against the coin whose own variance is smallest -- at the 50-fill floor it sits between two of the three per-coin shares rather than below all of them. The mechanism is the shared denominator: SOL's total per-cell variance is 5.0x at the 50-fill floor and 13.0x at the 100-fill floor of BTC's. Overlap works the same way and the population has to be named with it, because the populations disagree by a factor of four: 55.7% of the 151,558 wallets in the three-window panel touch exactly one coin, but only 12.4% of the 9,240 wallets that actually enter the pooled cell at the 50-fill floor do. Report the per-coin shares with the fill floor named beside them; treat the pooled share as a diluted lower bound only.
_meta.claim_note: The claim is that a STATISTICALLY SEPARABLE / IDENTIFIED wallet-idiosyncratic component of per-counterparty toxicity exists (positive after the cross-wallet covariance bias correction, reliability>0, label-permutation p in the right tail with BH-FDR control). The MAGNITUDE is a small share BECAUSE roughly half of the total per-cell variance is irreducible within-cell sampling noise (the 'within' component); a small identified share does NOT imply economic dominance and we do NOT claim the idiosyncratic part dominates toxicity.
_meta.common_leg_note: LIMITATION: the COMMON (period) leg is estimated on only THREE windows (202508/202510/202512), so Var(c_t) is under-identified and is EXCLUDED from the identification gate. The gate keys on the idiosyncratic leg only; the common share is reported for transparency, not claimed to be identified.
_meta.share_correction_method: corrected_idio_share_10s_print = corrected_idio_var_10s_print / total_var_10s_print; corrected_idio_var_10s_print is bias-corrected by the cross-wallet half-mean covariance estimator, NOT by Spearman-Brown disattenuation. Reliability is a diagnostic / >0 gate only.
_meta.field_suffix_note: Every level, variance, share and reliability below carries _10s_print: the window it was measured on and the reference price it was measured against. Counts, p-values and q-values do not, because they describe the test rather than the markout.

fdr_summary.method: sort ascending, q_(i) = p_(i) * m / i, running minimum from the largest p downward, clipped to 1; NaN p-values are carried through and excluded from the family size
fdr_summary.family: panel idiosyncratic placebo p-values across {BTC,ETH,SOL,pooled} x K
fdr_summary.threshold_meaning: the p-value cutoff actually applied: the largest rank k with p_(k) <= k*alpha/m, times alpha/m. With no rejection it is the rank-one bar the best cell failed
fdr_summary.q_note: the q-values are on the cells, under placebo_q_value_bh; this block holds the procedure, the family and the cutoff applied to them

naive.bias_note: idio_naive_var_10s_print = Var(a_i) + E[Var(u)/n_i] is UPWARD-biased; the split-half-corrected idiosyncratic variance (noise cancelled in the cross-wallet covariance) is in split_half_corrected

split_half_corrected.note: corrected_idio_var_10s_print = mean over seeds of Cov(aHat_A, aHat_B) across wallets, both halves period-demeaned by the SAME common FE; the within-cell noise cancels in the cross-wallet covariance

reliability.method: Spearman-Brown on period-demeaned odd/even split, averaged over the reliability seed's own splits (settings.RELIABILITY_SEED), not over the master seed's; DIAGNOSTIC / >0 gate only, NOT applied to the corrected share

procedure.method: permutation p = (draws at least as extreme + 1) / (usable draws + 1); the observed labelling counts as one draw of its own null, so p is floored at 1/(usable + 1) and is never zero

read_inputs.rule: TRUE requires corrected_idio_share_10s_print>0 AND reliability_10s_print>0 AND placebo p<=0.05 (BH-q across the family applied in _meta)
